blocks.text: Mastering Slack for business analysts on Mac

As a business analyst, your day involves constant context switching. You move from stakeholder interviews to Jira tickets to Slack messages. Slack is often the place where requirements change in real time. If you do not manage your channels, you will lose track of critical decisions.

Your Mac setup matters. Use the native Slack app rather than the browser version. The desktop app supports better keyboard shortcuts and notification handling. Version 4.53.x requires macOS 14 Sonoma or newer. Keeping your app updated ensures you get the latest search modifiers.

Searching for past decisions is a core part of your job. Use search modifiers to cut through the noise. Type in:channelname to narrow your scope. Use from:username to find what a specific developer said about a feature. If you forget a shortcut, press Command + / to see the full list.

items: Use Command + K to open the quick switcher for jumping between chats.
Use Command + G to search everything in your workspace.
Use Command + F to search only the current channel.
Use Shift + Enter to add line breaks to your long requirements messages.
Use Command + B for bold text when highlighting key constraints.

blocks.text: Threads are where business analysis happens. When you see a discussion about a requirement, jump into the thread immediately. Use the Threads view to see all your active conversations in one place. If a discussion is moving too fast, save the message for later using the ribbon icon.
If you find yourself repeating the same requirements to different stakeholders, create a snippet in Lazur. Use the dictation feature to draft your response and paste it into the Slack thread.
blocks.title: Save time on repetitive updates

blocks.text: Slack can become sluggish if you are in dozens of channels. If the app feels slow, do not just restart your Mac. Go to the menu bar and select Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This often fixes UI glitches and search latency.
Why use Lazur for Slack analysis

Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. It sees what you see. If you are stuck in a complex thread and need to find a specific decision from last week, hold Option + Command. Ask Lazur to find the message about the login flow. It will point you to the right channel or conversation.

Organize your channels by project phase. Use prefixes like proj-discovery-, proj-dev-, and proj-qa-. This makes it easier for your team to know where to post. If you need to mute a noisy channel, right click the channel name and select Mute. You can always check it later.

When stakeholders give feedback in Slack, treat it as a formal requirement. Use the pin feature to keep the agreed-upon scope visible in the channel. If you need to set a reminder for yourself to update a Jira ticket, use the Slack reminder feature. Type /remind followed by your task and the time.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Slack?
faq.answer: Lazur acts as a layer on top of your Mac. It does not integrate with Slack directly. You hold Option + Command to ask questions about your screen, and Lazur points at or answers questions about what you see in the Slack app.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to type messages in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold the fn key to dictate your messages. This is useful for typing out long requirements or complex feedback without needing to type manually.

faq.question: How do I find hidden channels in Slack?
faq.answer: Use the quick switcher with Command + K. If you still cannot find it, ask Lazur where the channel list is or how to browse all channels.

faq.question: Is it safe to use voice dictation for work requirements?
faq.answer: Lazur processes your voice and screen only while you hold the shortcut. Your data is not stored or used to train models.
